world.bio: I'm a second-year speech-language pathology student at UT Austin focused on augmentative and alternative communication (AAC). I grew up in San Antonio translating between English, Spanish and ASL for my deaf uncle at family dinners, and I think that is why I am happiest when a kid finds a way to say something new. I work weekends at a taco place on South Congress and I am saving for a trip to Oaxaca in the spring.
skills_assets: Second-year SLP graduate student focused on augmentative and alternative communication (AAC)
Conversational Spanish, working ASL, and a decent ear for how nonspeaking kids use gaze and gesture
Supervised practicum placements at an elementary school and a pediatric clinic, with hours logged toward the CCC
Access to her lab's 12 AAC tablets (iPads loaded with Proloquo2Go and TouchChat) for community events
A pile of laminated core-vocabulary boards she made at the print shop
Weekend taco-shop job, which means she can talk to anyone for six hours straight
Can sign basic ASL and uses it with nonspeaking kids as a bridge to symbols
A spreadsheet tracking every practicum hour, the supervisor who signed it, and the skills practiced, color coded by week
Good at explaining clinical terms to parents without jargon, which comes from translating for my uncle's doctor appointments

projects.name: Practicum hours
projects.text: I need 400 supervised clinical hours before graduation and I'm at about 190. Placements are limited, and my clinic supervisor Dr. Okafor has said that community events with nonspeaking kids can count if she signs off in advance. My lab has 12 AAC tablets that I can sign out for community events, and those hours count toward my practicum. I have been looking for something that isn't a classroom.

projects.name: Praxis prep
projects.text: The Praxis SLP exam is in November. I have a study group of four on Tuesdays and I am doing about 20 practice questions a day. Phonology and fluency disorders are my weak spots; I keep mixing up the types of dysfluency.

projects.name: Core vocabulary boards for the taco shop
projects.text: A small joke project: my boss let me make a pictorial ordering board for customers who don't speak much English or who use AAC. Not sure it will get used, but it is fun to design.

projects.name: Thesis literature review
projects.text: My capstone is a review of how often communication partners model on AAC devices in home versus school settings. I have 34 papers in a folder, 11 read, and a draft of the introduction I hate. My advisor wants an outline by October 25. I keep opening the doc and then opening Instagram instead. Trying to commit to one hour on Sunday mornings before the shift.

notes.text: Long day. Clinic in the morning, class at one, shift at five. Spilled queso on my scrubs and kept wearing them. A little girl at the clinic today used her tablet to say 'more' for the first time and her mom cried in the hallway. I almost did too.

Spent my lunch break on the library steps reading a paper on aided language stimulation. The idea is simple: you model the device yourself, pointing at symbols while you talk, the same way you'd talk to a baby who doesn't have words yet. Nobody ever expects the baby to be silent. Yet with AAC, we hand a kid the device and expect output with no input. I underlined that sentence twice and then got ketchup on it.
Dr. Okafor said my notes are too long. She wants SOAP notes in half a page. I've been writing like a diary. Trying to cut. Mija, she said, nobody reads a novel in a chart.

Saw a flyer for a free sensory-friendly movie morning at a theater in the north part of town. Lights up, sound down, kids can move around. I stood there thinking this is what everything should be like, a little looser around the edges. Took a photo of the flyer. Not sure why.

Called my uncle. He told me the same story about the bus driver who learned three signs just to say good morning. I've heard it a hundred times. I listened like it was new. （09-17补记）Praxis practice test: 71%. Bad on fluency. I keep confusing blocks and prolongations. Need flashcards. Maybe ask Jess to quiz me at the study group.

Grad school math: tuition after the stipend is about $11,000 a year, living costs $1,400 a month, taco shop pays $15.50 plus tips on a good night, maybe $80. I've done this calculation so many times I could do it in my sleep and sometimes I do. The Oaxaca trip is the one thing I am not cutting. It's the only line on the spreadsheet that isn't about surviving.

Oaxaca fund: $1,140. Flight is about $480 in March. Rent went up $50 this month. I told myself I would skip coffee. Lasted two days. （09-21补记）Called home. My dad answered, which never happens. He asked about the taco job and said he's proud that I work and study. He doesn't say that often. I told him it's mostly queso burns and tired feet. He said, 'Eso es honor.' I held the phone against my chest after we hung up for a second.

Observed a session with an eight-year-old who is nonspeaking. His grandmother says he has opinions about everything, he just can't get them out. Watched him hit the tablet to tell the therapist her shoes were ugly. We all laughed. That's communication.

The tablets in the lab are not being used on weekends. Lab manager said I can sign them out if I fill the form two days ahead and a faculty member is named. I think there's a lot of tablet time just sitting there.

Went to a farmers market in East Austin with Jess. There was a kids' booth where a boy, maybe six, kept pointing at a jar of honey and making a sound. His dad was guessing: 'Honey? Bee? Sweet?' None right. Then the boy pulled his dad's hand to the jar and tapped the lid. Open. Just open. I wanted to hand them a board so badly. I didn't, because I'm not allowed to treat a stranger's kid on a Saturday morning. But I thought about it for the rest of the day.

Weekend shift ended at 11. Boss gave me free tacos, I ate three in the car. My feet hurt. Sometimes I think I am trying to be two people: the one who sits with a kid for forty minutes and the one who yells 'order up!'

Practice Praxis question about a three-year-old with a phonological process of fronting. I got it right and felt unreasonably proud. Fronting: 'cat' becomes 'tat', 'go' becomes 'do'. Hearing it in my head with my cousin's voice, who did exactly this until she was four. Theory is just stories with names attached.
Mom texted that she is worried about my loans. I told her it will be fine. It will probably be fine. I have a plan, but also the plan is mostly that things will work out.

Weekend plan: study Saturday morning, shift Saturday evening, church with Mom on video Sunday, read thesis papers Sunday afternoon. No room for anything extra. But I keep thinking about whether I could take a few of those tablets to something outside the clinic. Hours I can count, kids I'd actually get to know. I'm not going to chase it until the Praxis is closer, but it's there.

messages.text:
Jess: Tuesday still on? I have the fluency flashcards.
Me: Yes. I'll bring pan dulce.
Jess: You're the best. Do you want to do a mock oral exam?
Me: God, no. But yes.

Dr. Okafor: Maya, your hours log is behind. You are at 190?
Me: Yes, and I'm looking for more.
Dr. Okafor: Community events can count if I sign off ahead of time. Send me details.
Me: Will do.

Daniela: Are you coming to the quinceañera in November? Tía says you owe her a dance.
Me: I'll be studying. I can come for the Saturday dinner.
Daniela: She will make you dance. Prepare.
Me: I will prepare my feet.

Mom: Are you eating? You sound tired.
Me: I'm fine. I eat tacos every day.
Mom: That is not a diet, mija.
Me: It's a lifestyle.

Dr. Chen: Maya, send me your outline by the 25th of October. Don't overthink.
Me: I'll send a draft. It will be rough.
Dr. Chen: Rough is fine. Just not missing.

Tío (signing via video): Your hands are getting faster.
Me: I've been practicing.
Tío: Come visit at Thanksgiving. I'll make tamales.
Me: I'll try.

Luis: You're on with me Saturday?
Me: Five to close.
Luis: Bring headphones, the speaker's broken.
Me: I always bring headphones. I study on break.

Boss: Maya, can you cover Saturday evening?
Me: I have a study session until four, can I come at five?
Boss: Five works. Thanks.
Me: Sure.

Priya: The tablets are all charged and updated. Remember the sign-out form has to be in two days before and it needs a faculty name.
Me: Dr. Okafor can sign. I'll send it Wednesday.
Priya: Also bring them back cleaned. Last time someone returned one with peanut butter on it.
Me: Gross. I'll sanitize.

Jess: Quiz me on voice disorders before Tuesday?
Me: Only if you quiz me on fluency.
Jess: Deal. Also, did you see that the Praxis registration deadline is the 20th?
Me: I paid already. $146 I'll never see again.
